old-behavior: module-import used plus + right-angle and accepted +⟩; source import used exact +> plus whitespace1; module-import-end always succeeded and extended a module identifier range
new-behavior: one import-sigil rule matches exact +>; module-import uses space-tab0; import-declaration uses space-tab1; module-import-end is removed; module identifier ranges end at the actual identifier
rationale: remove inconsistent sigil decomposition, accidental Unicode spelling, newline-after-sigil acceptance, and grammar-level range bookkeeping
Mech whitespace is intentionally permissive; a match question mark need not be adjacent to its preceding formula

old-behavior: counted operators accepted decimal literal counts only
new-behavior: bracketed matrix expressions supply singleton-broadcast or matching-shape per-element counts; literal shorthand retains whole-value iteration
rationale: unambiguous expression boundaries and independent scalar lanes without changing existing whole-carrier callbacks

new-behavior: underscore is accepted after an identifier start; exact names win and unresolved read names may select one visible unary catalog projection by receiver type
rationale: generic type-directed addressing sugar must preserve ordinary underscore bindings and normal canonical call authority

old-behavior: canonical title metadata admitted fields but omitted module imports supported since edb3f8e9a
new-behavior: title metadata admits ordinary module imports with code terminals alongside fields; imports retain root binding semantics and stay out of rendered chrome
rationale: restore the documented language design and original maintained EKF/N-body documents rather than moving authored imports

old-behavior: unordered/check-list sublists consumed a following underlined numbered heading as an ordered-list item; its dashed underline became a recovered unary expression
new-behavior: underlined subtitles retain section ownership before ordered-list item selection, including nested list candidates
rationale: section boundaries apply inside list alternatives as well as the outer document loop; preserve the original working bubble-sort example
